RAJYA  SABHA

List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, the December 5, 2001/Agrahayana 14, 1923 (Saka)

(Ministries: Coal and Mines; Defence; Home Affairs;  Non-Conventional
Energy Sources; Power, Rural Development; Textiles)
Total number of questions145
WIN2\SESSION\3693RS
1
Budgetary support for the
development of North-Eastern States
1665. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of COAL AND MINES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has chalked
out its own Action Plan for the progress of
North-Eastern Region and removal of
industrial backwardness there, keeping in
view the directive issued by the Ministry
of Finance and Planning Commission to all
the Ministries including Ministry of Coal
and Mines for spending 10 per cent of gross
budgetary support for development of
North-Eastern States; and
(b) if so, the details of the steps taken
for implementation of the Action Plan and
removal of industrial backwardness?
Joint ventures taken up by CIL for the
production of coal
1666. SHRI SOLIPETA
RAMACHANDRA REDDY: Will the
Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Coal India Ltd. is taking up
new projects through joint venture for
production of coal;
(b) if so, how far the production
capacity is expected to be expanded; and
(c) the steps taken to invite participants
and the details of willing participants?
Production of Aluminium
1667. SHRI ANANTA SETHI: Will the
Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) the efforts made by Government to
increase the production of Aluminium and
alumina;
(b) the achievement made in this regard
in Eighth and Ninth Plans; and
(c) the details of the contribution of
NALCO thereto?
Gold and Copper Mines discovered
near Ajmer
1668. SHRI R. P. GOENKA: Will the
Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that gold and
copper mines have been discovered near
Ajmer in Hathipur village of Shrinagar
Panchayat Samiti, as reported in the Asian
Age dated 2nd September, 2001;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken to protect the
specific potential geographical zone and
adjoining areas against unlawful
excavations?

2
WIN2\SESSION\3693RS 2
Sign of land subsidence in the coal
mines areas of Dhanbad
1669. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that large areas of
coal mines, particularly in the district of
Dhanbad in Jharkhand have been showing
consistent sign of land subsidence;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
approximate number of population in these
areas facing threats of land subsidence;
(c) whether Government are
implementing any programme for shifting
and rehabilitation of the affected people
residing in these endangered areas to a safer
place and arresting such subsidence in
Jharkhand; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Aluminium metal production by
recycling the scrap
1670. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of primary
Aluminium metal production made by
recycling the scrap in the year 2000-2001;
(b) how it compares with the World
figures; and
(c) the quantity of Aluminium scrap
imported during last three years and how
the use of imported scrap compares with
the domestic scrap in respect of Aluminium
metal production through recycling
process?
Ash pond disaster of NALCO in
Angul, Orissa
1671. SHRI MAN MOHAN SAMAL:
Will the Minister of COAL AND MINES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have assessed
the losses caused by the ash pond disaster
of NALCO on 31st December, 2000 in the
Angul district of Orissa;
(b) if so, the area-wise/family-wise/
village-wise details of the loss caused;
(c) whether compensation has been
given to the affected people; and
(d) if so, the area-wise/family-wise/
village-wise details thereof?
Corruption in CIL and its subsidiaries
1672. SHRI KRISHNA KUMAR
BIRLA: Will the Minister of COAL AND
MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether in view of widespread
corruption in CIL and its subsidiaries, the
Government propose to bring major
administrative changes in CIL and its
subsidiaries;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have received
reports against a large number of officials
of CII and its subsidiaries;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the details of steps taken by
Government to bring transparency in the
functioning of CIL and its subsidiaries?
Financial bunglings in CIL
1673. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the
Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Management of Coal
India Limited has spent several crores on
legal expenses during the last few years
and shown these spending as miscellaneous
expenses in its account books;
(b) if so, the facts and details thereof;
(c) whether the financial bunglings in
CIL and  its subsidiaries have increased
and there is no machinery to check it; and
